messages:
Dev Patel: pulling some patterns from recent onboarding tickets (last ~3 weeks). want to make sure the Console checklist + step copy preempts the most common faceplants.

Top issues:
1) 401s: wrong key type/env (test vs prod), key copied with whitespace, org vs project mismatch. SUP-9244 is a clean example.
2) 429s: folks hit default rate limits / daily quota while running quickstart in a loop, then think "API is down". SUP-9182.
3) streaming disconnects: SSE client defaults, proxies, missing keepalive, retry logic not streaming-safe. SUP-9210.
4) timeouts: default HTTP client timeout too low + no retry/backoff, esp when first call does cold-ish path.
5) CORS: calling from browser directly; some assume they can do client-side fetch from prod website.
6) confusion around "what is production" / when to rotate keys.

Suggestion: checklist needs explicit wording + deep links to troubleshooting + rate limits page. also maybe a tiny callout that Redwood API keys are server-side.

Priya Shah: +1. 401s are THE thing. people paste the key with quotes or a trailing newline too.

I’d propose we add a step (or subtext) that literally says:
- “Create a **test** API key for local dev (restricted). Create a **prod** key only when deploying server-side.”
- “If you see 401, confirm you’re using the right key + project + base URL.”

Also a microcopy line on the key page: “Keys won’t work from the browser.”

Nikhil Sharma: super helpful. we’re already planning a “prod vs test key” step, but copy like this is gold. do we want to include "org vs project" in the checklist or too in-the-weeds?

Dev Patel: I’d keep checklist copy simple but add a 401 tooltip/learn-more that mentions:
- key env mismatch (test/prod)
- key revoked/rotated
- project not selected (or using a key from different project)
- whitespace/newlines

We can link it to the troubleshooting page (docs) so support isn’t rewriting the same thing.

Marissa Cole: question: can we do any validation on 401s to auto-nudge? like detect repeated 401s in the request logs and surface a banner?

Dylan Brooks: technically yes (gateway logs → “auth_failed” events) but we need to be careful about privacy + not spamming. also lag. might be Phase 2-ish.

Priya Shah: even without auto-detect, the step should warn about 429.
Proposed wording for the “Rate limits & quotas” step:
Title: “Know your quotas (avoid 429s)”
Body: “Check your project’s rate limits and free-tier quotas. If you get a 429, back off and retry with jitter. Don’t loop the quickstart at full speed.”
CTA: “View quotas” → console quotas page
Secondary link: “429 troubleshooting” → docs

Nikhil Sharma: love “don’t loop the quickstart at full speed” lol. might need a slightly more neutral tone, but sentiment is right.

Elliot Price: if we’re linking to docs for these, we should standardize the CTA labels + UTM params so we can attribute which steps are actually clicked. (we have a docs deep-link convention doc in flight)

Wei Chen: on docs side, I can make sure the troubleshooting section has anchors for 401 / 429 / streaming disconnects so checklist can deep link directly.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: on 401: we should be explicit that there are different keys (test vs prod) AND that prod keys might be restricted by IP allowlist (if enabled) → which can also look like auth failure from their perspective.

Dev Patel: good call. that comes up with a few teams. but maybe keep the checklist step to “create the right key” and then the doc link covers IP allowlisting.

Priya Shah: streaming disconnects: biggest cause I see is people using fetch() and not reading the stream properly, or corporate proxy closing idle connections.
Checklist step copy idea:
Title: “Try streaming (and handle disconnects)”
Body: “Enable streaming responses and implement reconnect + retry. Expect occasional disconnects; don’t treat them as fatal.”
CTA: “Streaming examples”
Secondary: “Troubleshoot SSE disconnects”

Dylan Brooks: +1, but we should be careful promising “reconnect” semantics. we don’t support resume-from-token in v1. maybe we phrase as “retry idempotently where possible” and “gracefully degrade to non-streaming.”

Marissa Cole: for checklist, we can phrase as: “Implement streaming with a fallback to non-streaming” (or “handle partial output”).

Nikhil Sharma: what about the browser/CORS one? do we add a step or just a gotcha callout?

Dev Patel: IMO a callout under “Make your first request” step:
“Calls should originate from a trusted server environment. Do not embed API keys in client-side apps.”
and link to “Client-side security” doc.

Priya Shah: also add “set timeouts + retries” somewhere. lots of folks are using default requests timeout (or none) and then complaining. I’d rather we push a clear best-practice.

Nikhil Sharma: we’ve debated whether “retries/timeouts” is its own step vs part of “first production launch”. support POV?

Dev Patel: support POV: put a minimal version earlier. like a step between “first request” and “first production launch”:
Title: “Add retries + timeouts”
Body: “Set a request timeout and implement exponential backoff retries for transient errors (429/5xx/timeouts).”
CTA: “Copy retry snippet (Python/TS/Go)”

If it’s buried in prod checklist, people won’t see it until after they already got burned.

Elliot Price: ok, if we do that, docs needs canonical snippets per SDK that compile. we can align with Monica/Ibrahim.

Marissa Cole: action items I’m hearing:
- Support to drop proposed step copy into the copy doc (or paste here and we’ll port).
- Docs to add anchors for the top error modes.
- PM/Design to ensure checklist step ordering includes retries/timeouts earlier.

Dev Patel: I’ll paste cleaned-up proposed microcopy here (feel free to edit tone):
1) “Create an API key” → “Create a test key for local dev. When you’re ready to deploy, create a prod key and keep it server-side.”
2) “Make your first request” → callout: “If you see a 401, confirm you copied the key exactly and you’re using the right project.”
3) “Add retries + timeouts” → “Set timeouts and retry with exponential backoff + jitter for 429/5xx/timeouts.”
4) “Know your quotas (avoid 429s)” → “Check your project’s quotas and rate limits. Back off on 429s; don’t run tight loops.”
5) “Try streaming” → “Use streaming for lower latency UX. Handle disconnects gracefully and consider a non-streaming fallback.”

:thumbsup: if this matches the direction.

Priya Shah: :thumbsup: also + “Do not call the API directly from the browser” somewhere prominent.

Nikhil Sharma: :thumbsup: from me. I’ll bring this into the PRD + DES copy ticket. thanks y’all.

Wei Chen: I’ll update troubleshooting doc draft to ensure each of those has a direct link target.

Dylan Brooks: and I’ll check with Logan/Nadia on whether we can at least *track* repeated 401/429 during onboarding (without content) for future validation/nudges.

Dev Patel: awesome. this will cut support volume a lot if we get it right.
